observation_summary: The cumulativeProbability method in NormalDistributionImpl throws a MaxIterationsExceededException when the input x is far from the mean, causing convergence issues in the underlying Erf calculation.
reasoning_summary: The fix introduces a try-catch block to handle the MaxIterationsExceededException. It adds conditional logic (guards) to check if the input x is sufficiently far from the mean (beyond 20 standard deviations) to return 0.0 or 1.0 instead of failing. This is a classic case of adding missing validation/guard logic to handle edge cases that the original algorithm could not converge on.
evidence_used: The fix adds a try-catch block around the Erf.erf call.
The catch block implements conditional checks (if/else if) to determine if the input x is outside a valid range (mean +/- 20 * standardDeviation).
The bug report states that the CDF should effectively be 0 or 1 in these extreme cases, which the new logic now enforces.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix modifies the procedure, the core issue is the lack of a guard/check for extreme input values that cause the existing algorithm to fail. The fix is primarily about adding conditional validation logic.
